item.title: The Texas Yogurt Shop Exonerations | Case by Case
item.description: For decades, Maurice Pierce, Robert Springsteen, Michael Scott and Forrest Welborn lived under the shadow of the yogurt shop murders, a crime that left an indelible mark on Austin and forever changed the lives of the the families of the victims: Eliza Thomas, Amy Ayers, and sisters Jennifer and Sarah Harbison. All four men were ultimately declared innocent and later exonerated after investigators linked another man to the killings. After reporting on this case for more 30 years, "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty speaks with Pierce's widow and daughter about the devastating toll of a wrongful accusation, their family's fight to clear his name, a financial settlement, and what justice means when it arrives decades too late.

item.title: Survivor Finalist Joe Hunter's Fight for Justice | Case by Case
item.description: During his time competing on "Survivor," Joe Hunter has been open about seeking justice for the death of his sister Joanna whose death was ruled a suicide. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and producer Michelle Fanucci discuss their investigation into Joanna's death and an interview with Hunter who believes Joanna's husband, former pastor Mark Lewis, staged the scene after years of domestic violence. Mark Lewis has not been charged with any crime relating to the death of Joanna.

item.title: The Trial of Larry Millete Begins | Case by Case
item.description: After years of waiting, Larry Millete's murder trial is underway in San Diego. He is accused of killing his wife, Maya Millete, who disappeared in 2021. The first week has already delivered bombshell testimony. In this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and CBS 8 San Diego reporter Kelly Hessedal break down the 2021 disappearance of Maya before diving into the stunning allegations laid out in court – including an alleged affair and emails with online spellcasters.

item.title: How a County Clerk Upended the Alex Murdaugh Case | Case by Case
item.description: The South Carolina Supreme Court just issued a stunning unanimous ruling overturning the 2023 double murder convictions of Alex Murdaugh. In this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and University of South Carolina School of Law professor Colin Miller break down the jury tampering allegations against Becky Hill that sent this notorious case back to square one.

item.title: Deadly Vacations | Case by Case
item.description: Why are so many dream vacations turning into true crime headlines? On the premiere episode of "Case by Case," we examine the trial of Gerhardt Konig, the former anesthesiologist found guilty of attempted manslaughter after a brutal cliffside attack on his wife Arielle in Hawaii. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman break down the trial's most stunning moments before diving into the chilling trend of headlines about vacations that turned deadly. From the ridges of Oahu to the waters of the Bahamas, we'll follow it all, "Case by Case."

item.title: Consulting AI for Murder | Case by Case
item.description: Last week, the remains of the second victim in the slaying of two University of South Florida students were finally identified. Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy were both doctoral candidates from Bangladesh. Hisham Abugharbieh, Limon's roommate, has been charged with two counts of first-degree murder in connection to their deaths. On this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and Miami-based CBS News correspondent Cristian Benavides break down what we know so far, and how, according to prosecutors, the suspected killer consulted AI to help plan the crimes. Limon and Bristy will both receive posthumous degrees on Friday.

item.title: Watch Live: Second psychiatric nurse practitioner testifies at Lindsay Clancy trial
item.description: Testimony at the Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Massachusetts will resume Tuesday with testimony from a second psychiatric nurse practitioner.

item.title: U.S. and Iran close to "peace arrangement or a deal," Pakistan says
item.description: The U.S. and Iran are close to agreeing on "some sort of arrangement," Pakistan's defense minister told Bloomberg on Tuesday.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Reece Weaver announces her Broadway debut
item.description: Reece Weaver, whose exit from the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders on the show "America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders" left viewers shocked, exclusively announced on "CBS Mornings" that she is making her Broadway debut. She talks about the transition, why she made the decision and what it was like to start rehearsals.

item.title: Airline rule changes you should know if you're planning to travel
item.description: Despite the back-to-school sales, it's still summer travel season. Kris Van Cleave explains some airline rule changes that could impact your wallet when you fly.

item.title: Flames shoot out of plane's engine after apparent bird strike
item.description: An American Airlines plane bound for North Carolina was forced to return to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, when flames erupted from its left engine due to an apparent bird strike.

item.title: Video of Arkansas trooper punching 18-year-old draws calls for investigation
item.description: Alisa Hackett, 18, was pulled over for speeding and alcohol possession when she was tackled to the ground and punched.

item.title: Powerball jackpot grows to staggering $975 million with UK players adding to sum
item.description: The Powerball jackpot has grown to a stunning $975 million, and players in the United Kingdom are now eligible to play. Powerball Product Group's Stephen Durrell explains how the lottery is evolving.

item.title: Newly released video shows Arkansas state trooper punching Black woman during traffic stop
item.description: Newly released video of a recent traffic stop in Arkansas shows a state trooper punching an 18-year-old Black woman in the face after forcing her to the ground on the side of a highway. The trooper said the woman was resisting arrest. Warning, the video may be disturbing.

item.title: Meta's Mark Zuckerberg thinks AI model code should be open to all
item.description: Facebook co-founder and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg argues that artificial intelligence should be open source to improve accessibility. CNET reporter Katelyn Chedraoui has more on what the philosophy of open source technology means in the AI era.

item.title: Darline Graham gets Trump support in South Carolina's primary to replace Lindsey Graham
item.description: In South Carolina's crowded special primary, Darline Graham, sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, is showcasing her coveted endorsement from President Trump. CBS News senior national correspondent Mark Strassmann has the latest from Columbia, South Carolina.

item.title: Fact-checking medical claims after Trump's new order on childhood vaccine recommendations
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order recommending that parents spread out vaccination schedules for their children, alleging an unproven connection with autism. CBS News' Dr. Céline Gounder has more.

item.title: How Trump was secretly moved between planes after Iran's missile threat
item.description: President Trump secretly moved between Air Force One and a military aircraft in Turkey after a missile threat from Iran, a U.S. official said. CBS News' Nancy Cordes explains what we know.

item.title: Despair, hope in Colombia as rescue teams comb debris for earthquake survivors
item.description: The powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake that hit Colombia was the strongest recorded in the last century, local officials said. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more on the urgent search for those who may be trapped under rubble.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Mornings Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Behind Zuckerberg's essay on the future of AI and what he calls the "most dangerous" scenario
item.description: Despite concerns about AI, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has an optimistic vision for its future, which he shared in a new essay. He also described what he thinks is the "most dangerous" AI scenario. Nick Thompson, CEO of The Atlantic, breaks down Zuckerberg's essay.

item.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak viewing on Wednesday night
item.description: The Perseid meteor shower is the best viewing all year, according to NASA.

item.title: One of Southern California's biggest entertainment hubs has become a battleground over big-money billboards
item.description: Billboards in Inglewood are at the heart of a high-stakes battle over advertising revenue, control of city finances and political influence as the city prepares to host massive crowds for upcoming events.

item.title: 5 takeaways from Zuckerberg's essay on his vision for superintelligence
item.description: In a 6,500-word post, the Meta CEO argues that superintelligence should be shared "with as many people and businesses as possible."

item.title: As Medicare pays less for cataract surgery, doctors turn to moneymaking lasers
item.description: More cataract patients, wanting not only restored but improved vision, are paying extra for their doctors to use a laser when a scalpel would do.

item.title: Rescuers race to find Colombia earthquake survivors as death toll rises
item.description: More than 2,700 people were reported missing on Monday night, after the country was struck by its strongest earthquake on record.

item.title: Trump secretly switched to different plane in Turkey amid Iran threat
item.description: Ahead of a flight from Turkey, President Trump secretly left Air Force One and was moved to another plane with the help of a catering truck, according to a source, as the U.S. grappled with a threat from Iran.

item.title: Congo Ebola death toll tops 2,000 in fastest spreading outbreak on record
item.description: At least 2,000 people have died among the confirmed cases in Congo's Ebola outbreak that is the fastest-spreading on record, according to the latest government data.

item.title: Powerball jackpot nears $1 billion after no one won $905 million grand prize
item.description: No winning tickets were sold for Monday night's $905 million Powerball jackpot, so the estimated grand prize for Wednesday night's drawing will be at least $975 million, Powerball says.

item.title: Hunter Biden says his father's cancer has spread
item.description: In a wide-ranging interview with the CBS News partner BBC News, Hunter Biden grew emotional as he discussed his father's condition, describing it as very sad to watch.
